headline: US October Employment Exceeds Forecasts as Unemployment Rate Falls to 4.1%
summary: The US economy added more jobs than expected in October, while the unemployment rate declined to 4.1%, signaling renewed labor market strength.
why: Employment data is a primary indicator of economic health and wage growth, heavily influencing Federal Reserve monetary policy decisions.

impacts.name: S&P 500
impacts.why: Stronger-than-expected jobs data shifts expectations for Federal Reserve rate hikes.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: Stronger employment numbers increase expectations of Federal Reserve interest rate hikes.
